# Psalm 92 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day. It's wonderful to thank the LORD, to sing praises to your name, Most High God!

**2** It's wonderful to announce your faithful love every morning and proclaim your reliability every night,

**3** accompanied by a ten-stringed harp and the melody of a lyre.

**4** LORD, you've made me so happy by what you've done! I sing for joy because of everything your hands have created.

**5** LORD, how amazing are your works! How incredibly deep are your thoughts!

**6** An ignorant person doesn't know this, and a fool can't grasp it:

**7** Even though the wicked pop up like weeds and evildoers seem to thrive — they're headed for eternal destruction.

**8** But you, LORD — you are exalted forever!

**9** Look at your enemies, LORD — your enemies will be destroyed! Every evildoer will be scattered.

**10** But you've lifted my strength high like a wild ox; you've poured fresh, fragrant oil on me.

**11** I've watched my enemies fall; I've heard the defeat of those who attacked me.

**12** Those who live right will thrive like palm trees and grow tall like the cedars of Lebanon.

**13** Planted right in the LORD's house, they'll flourish in the courtyards of our God.

**14** Even in old age they'll still produce fruit — they'll stay vital and green,

**15** showing everyone that the LORD is just. He is my rock, and there's not a trace of injustice in him.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **92:7**: This verse flips the script on envy: when the wicked thrive, it's not success — it's the calm before the storm. Weeds grow fast, but they don't last.

- **92:12-14**: What a counter to our culture's obsession with youth! The righteous 'still bear fruit in old age.' God's people don't peak and decline — they keep growing, like cedars that take centuries to mature.

— PNEUMA
